item.title: Dell warns of critical root privilege escalation vulnerability CVE-2026-86360 in Dell System Update CLI
item.description:
Enterprise hardware management advisories published today detail emergency security updates for a critical privilege escalation flaw in server deployment toolkits. Local unprivileged users can exploit temporary file creation routines to execute arbitrary operating system commands under root administrative privileges.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-86360, affects Dell System Update DSU command-line interface tools managing PowerEdge server deployments. The security flaw stems from insecure temporary file permission handling during firmware package extraction. Local unprivileged attackers manipulate symbolic links in temporary execution directories, forcing the privileged installation daemon to execute malicious binaries with elevated root rights. Official advisories urge server administrators to update command-line deployment utilities across Linux and Windows server hosts immediately.
Subverting hardware management deployment tools undermines operating system security boundaries across enterprise server fleets. When local threat actors escalate privileges to root via hardware utilities, adversaries gain capabilities to unhook endpoint protection agents, modify system kernel modules, and establish persistent footholds across datacenter infrastructure.
- Upgrade Dell System Update DSU installations immediately to official fixed release builds published by vendor engineering. - Restrict unprivileged local interactive user rights and execution permissions on Linux and Windows server hosts. - Inspect system temporary execution directories for anomalous symbolic link creations or unverified binary drops. - Enforce strict file system integrity monitoring across server deployment scripts and management utilities.
Server hardware toolchain defense demands rapid utility patch deployment and strict file system access controls to ensure enterprise management software remains insulated from local root privilege escalation. #CodeDefence #Dell #PowerEdge #PrivilegeEscalation #Root #EndpointSecurity #AppSec #PatchManagement

item.title: Active mass scanning targets Rejetto HTTP File Server weak key RCE vulnerability CVE-2026-61500
item.description:
Network threat monitoring arrays confirm active global scanning sweeps targeting a high-severity session handling vulnerability in lightweight web file server software. Unauthenticated remote adversaries exploit weak cryptographic signing keys to forge administrative cookies and execute remote code.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-61500, affects Rejetto HTTP File Server HFS releases. The defect arises from the use of static or predictable session signing keys within session token generation modules. Unauthenticated remote adversaries transmit forged HTTP authorization headers to bypass authentication logic, obtaining administrative access over target servers and executing arbitrary system commands. Threat telemetry indicates automated botnets actively scanning internet-facing HFS instances to drop crypto-miners and reverse proxies.
Subverting web file server daemons exposes stored enterprise files and host network boundaries. When unauthenticated actors achieve remote code execution on file server hosts, adversaries can exfiltrate sensitive corporate files, deploy secondary malware payloads, and pivot into internal network segments.
- Apply official maintenance security updates across all Rejetto HTTP File Server deployments immediately. - Restrict public internet access to file management web interfaces by placing hosts behind zero-trust access proxies. - Inspect HTTP server access logs for unverified administrative session requests or anomalous cookie structures. - Isolate file server hosting roots on dedicated subnets and restrict outbound network connectivity to untrusted domains.
Web file server security relies on robust cryptographic session signing and strict access control isolation to ensure lightweight file management daemons remain protected from unauthenticated remote takeover. #CodeDefence #Rejetto #HFS #RCE #SessionForgery #WebSecurity #AppSec #ThreatIntelligence

item.title: FBI removes contractor following ShinyHunters breach of Oracle PeopleSoft job portal via WAF bypass CVE-2026-35273
item.description:
Incident response investigations published today detail law enforcement actions following a major breach of federal job applicant databases. The intrusion was enabled by third-party patch management failures that left enterprise software endpoints vulnerable to web application firewall bypass techniques.
The security incident involved federal portal infrastructure built on Oracle PeopleSoft. Threat actors belonging to the ShinyHunters group exploited vulnerability CVE-2026-35273 targeting Environment Management Hub PSEMHUB endpoints. The attackers utilized URL-encoding manipulation to evade web application firewall rules, accessing backend databases and exfiltrating personal information belonging to thousands of agency employees and applicants. Federal authorities confirmed the removal of the responsible maintenance contractor alongside ongoing law enforcement investigations.
Failing to apply vendor security patches while relying exclusively on perimeter firewall rules creates catastrophic supply chain exposure. When threat actors bypass firewall pattern-matching rules, unpatched backend enterprise applications remain fully exposed to unauthenticated data exfiltration.
- Force immediate patch application published by Oracle across all PeopleSoft application server deployments. - Reconfigure web application firewall inspection engines to perform complete URI path decoding prior to evaluating security rules. - Conduct continuous third-party vendor patch compliance audits across managed government and corporate application infrastructure. - Restrict network routing to administrative endpoints like PSEMHUB, placing management interfaces on isolated internal VLANs.
Enterprise supply chain risk governance requires strict patch execution verification and multi-layered access controls to ensure critical application portals remain insulated from perimeter firewall bypass techniques. #CodeDefence #Oracle #PeopleSoft #ShinyHunters #WAFBypass #SupplyChain #DataExfiltration #IncidentResponse #AppSec
